policies.title: Positive Airway Pressure (PAP) Devices for Obstructive Sleep Apnea

criteria.name: Diagnostic Polysomnography (AHI/RDI)
criteria.cms_document: CMS DME MAC LCD L33829 (Positive Airway Pressure Devices for OSA)
criteria.source_section: Coverage Indications, Limitations, and/or Medical Necessity - Initial Coverage
criteria.source_paragraph: Paragraph 1: AHI or RDI >= 15 events/hr, or AHI/RDI >= 5 and <= 14 with documented comorbid hypertension, stroke, or daytime sleepiness
criteria.source_text_excerpt: An initial positive airway pressure device is covered for beneficiaries with an AHI or RDI >= 15 events per hour, or an AHI or RDI >= 5 and <= 14 events per hour with documented symptoms of excessive daytime sleepiness, impaired cognition, mood disorders, or insomnia, or documented hypertension, ischemic heart disease, or history of stroke.

criteria.name: Face-to-Face Clinical Evaluation
criteria.cms_document: CMS DME MAC LCD L33829 (Positive Airway Pressure Devices for OSA)
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Prior to the sleep test, the beneficiary must have a face-to-face clinical evaluation by the treating physician or practitioner to assess the patient for obstructive sleep apnea.

policies.title: Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy for Diabetic Wounds of Lower Extremities

criteria.name: Severe Diabetic Wound Wagner Grade 3 or Higher
criteria.source_paragraph: Paragraph 4: Diabetic wounds of the lower extremities in patients who have Wagner grade III or higher lesions
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Diabetic wounds of the lower extremities in patients who have Wagner grade III or higher lesions.

criteria.name: Failure of >= 30 Days Standard Conservative Wound Therapy
criteria.source_paragraph: Paragraph 4: Prerequisite Failure of Standard Wound Therapy
criteria.source_text_excerpt: The patient must have completed at least 30 continuous days of standard wound therapy without evidence of measurable signs of healing.

criteria.name: Lower Extremity Vascular Assessment
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Evaluation of lower extremity vascular status and treatment of any treatable vascular problem.

criteria.name: Severe Aortic Stenosis Hemodynamic Threshold
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis (AVA <= 1.0 cm2 or mean aortic gradient >= 40 mmHg or peak velocity >= 4.0 m/s).

criteria.name: Heart Team Consultation
criteria.source_text_excerpt: A multidisciplinary team (heart team) that includes a cardiac surgeon and an interventional cardiologist who have independently evaluated the patient.

criteria.name: Procedural Futility Exclusion
criteria.source_text_excerpt: TAVR is non-covered when procedural futility exists due to severe non-cardiac conditions with life expectancy < 1 year or terminal comorbid illness.

criteria.name: Prohibitive Surgical or Anatomical Contraindication Exclusion
criteria.source_paragraph: Paragraph 2: Prohibitive Surgical and Anatomical Contraindications
criteria.source_text_excerpt: TAVR is non-covered for patients with prohibitive anatomical contraindications or uncontrolled systemic sepsis.

criteria.name: Severe LV Systolic Dysfunction (LVEF <= 35%)
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Patients with documented left ventricular ejection fraction <= 35% on diagnostic imaging.

criteria.name: Heart Failure Functional Classification (NYHA II/III)
criteria.source_paragraph: Paragraph 1(b): NYHA Class II or III functional symptoms
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Patients with New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class II or III heart failure symptoms.

criteria.name: Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy Duration (>=90 Days)
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Patients must have received optimal guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure for at least 3 months.

criteria.name: Cardiomyopathy Etiology & Revascularization Timeline
criteria.source_text_excerpt: At least 40 days must have elapsed after acute myocardial infarction, or at least 90 days after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

criteria.name: Cardiogenic Shock or Terminal Illness Exclusion
criteria.source_text_excerpt: CMS does not cover ICD implantation for patients in cardiogenic shock, or with non-cardiac disease with life expectancy less than 1 year.

policies.title: Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty (PTA) with Carotid Artery Stenting (CAS)

criteria.name: Severe Carotid Stenosis (>= 70% Symptomatic or >= 80% Asymptomatic)
criteria.source_text_excerpt: FDA-approved carotid stent systems and FDA-approved embolic protection devices for patients with symptomatic carotid artery stenosis >= 70% or asymptomatic stenosis >= 80%.

criteria.name: Documented High Surgical Risk for Carotid Endarterectomy (CEA)
criteria.source_paragraph: Paragraph b: High Surgical Risk for Carotid Endarterectomy
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Patients who are at high risk for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) due to significant medical comorbidities or anatomically unfavorable neck features.

criteria.name: Mandatory FDA-Approved Embolic Protection Device (EPD)
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Coverage is contingent upon the mandatory deployment of an FDA-approved distal embolic protection device.

policies.title: Percutaneous Left Atrial Appendage Closure (LAAC / Watchman)

criteria.name: Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation with High Stroke Risk (CHA2DS2-VASc >= 3)
criteria.source_paragraph: Paragraph 1: Non-Valvular Atrial Fibrillation with Stroke Risk
criteria.source_text_excerpt: A CHADS2 score >= 2 or CHA2DS2-VASc score >= 3 indicating high stroke risk in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation.

criteria.name: Contraindication to Long-Term Oral Anticoagulation (HAS-BLED >= 3)
criteria.source_text_excerpt: A formal clinical rationale establishing that the patient is unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulation.

criteria.name: Pre-Procedural Imaging Verifying Absence of LA Thrombus
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Pre-procedural imaging confirming the absence of intracardiac thrombus prior to transcatheter transseptal puncture.

criteria.name: Resting Hypoxemia (PaO2 <= 55 mmHg or SpO2 <= 88%)
criteria.source_section: Section B: Group I Medical Documentation Requirements
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Arterial blood gas PaO2 at or below 55 mm Hg, or an arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2) at or below 88% measured at rest.

criteria.name: Clinical Stability at Evaluation
criteria.source_text_excerpt: The qualifying arterial blood gas study or oximetry test was conducted in a chronic, clinically stable state.

criteria.name: Acute Reversible Etiology Exclusion
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Oxygen therapy is non-covered for conditions where hypoxemia is transient or reversible by standard treatment.
